issues.quote: Madame plays well. I have heard her many times, and I know the sound of her hands on the keys.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that the household heard Madame's piano begin and stop by the kitchen clock. It does not say who was playing.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this to mean Madame was the one playing from 10:48 to 11:01, which gives her a whereabouts and an alibi-relevant identity the sheet never supplies.

issues.quote: It is a minute repeater, so when you press the slide it speaks the time. The hours come in low notes. Each quarter is a doubled note. The minutes past the quarter come in high notes. He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The sheet says nothing about a repeater, its chimes, or any strike the master meant to make. None of the listed readings depend on sound.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a way to decode times from heard chimes, or as a hint that a chime was heard at some moment, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: She keeps it that way on purpose, so that nothing in her kitchen is ever late.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that Rosa's clock was exactly fifteen minutes fast.
issues.misreading: The deliberate-setting detail is unsupported. It does not change the reading, but it adds a claim the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: I regulated it myself, and I know what it does.
issues.fact: The sheet says only that her watch was exact at the dinner check.
issues.misreading: It adds a claim about her own expertise and knowledge of her watch's behaviour that the sheet does not give. It does not alter any reading.
